questions.question: In CrossAttention.forward, which tensors supply queries versus keys and values?
options: Image memory supplies Q; text x supplies K and V
Both Q and K come from text, while V is a learned scalar
Text x supplies Q; image memory supplies K and V
Q, K, and V are all projected from the concatenated sequence
questions.explanation: The method applies q_proj to x, the text stream, and project_memory to memory, the image stream. Thus text length is the query length and image-token length is the key/value length.

questions.question: In a decoder block with both self-attention and cross-attention, which one uses a causal mask?
options: Both
Cross-attention only
Neither
Self-attention only; the image is fully observed and cross-attention has no temporal order
questions.explanation: Text generation is autoregressive, so text self-attention is causal. Image tokens are all visible before any text is decoded.

questions.question: Why is the cross-attention KV cache built once per image?
options: Image keys and values do not change as text is decoded, so projecting memory once and reusing the K and V across all decode steps is the whole inference speedup
PyTorch requires caching
Caching saves disk space
It avoids using the GPU
questions.explanation: The vision encoder runs once. Its KV projection is computed once. Each text token reuses the cache for free.

questions.question: What is the output shape of cross-attention when text length is Nt=10 and image length is Nv=197 with hidden=256?
questions.explanation: Cross-attention output shape follows the query stream, so output is (B, Nt, hidden) regardless of key length.

questions.question: Why is no mask used on cross-attention?
options: Masks are too expensive
PyTorch does not support cross masks
The image is fully observed before text generation begins; every text position may attend to every patch
Masks always cause NaN
questions.explanation: There is no temporal order on image patches and no leakage to prevent, so cross-attention sees the whole image.

questions.question: Which residual computation matches the documented learned gate extension for cross-attention?
options: x = tanh(x + cross_attn(x, memory)) and the residual is discarded
x = x + softmax(gate) * self_attn(x), with no image memory
x = cross_attn(x, memory) and the text residual is always removed
x = x + tanh(gate) * cross_attn(x, memory), with gate initialized at zero
questions.explanation: The lesson's baseline has no gate, but its extension scales the cross-attention residual by tanh(gate). A zero-initialized gate starts near the text-only path and can learn to open the image path.
